scenarioStory.history: Sudden onset of severe substernal chest pressure approximately 45 minutes ago while resting in his recliner watching TV. Pain radiates to the left arm and jaw, rated 9/10, associated with diaphoresis and nausea. Denies exertion at onset. Denies use of sildenafil, tadalafil, or vardenafil.
scenarioStory.course: Initial Contact: Crew arrives to find a 60-year-old male seated in a recliner, pale and diaphoretic, clutching his chest. He reports crushing chest pain radiating to his left arm and jaw for the past 45 minutes. → 12-lead, ASA, and IV started: 12-lead EKG confirms an inferior STEMI. Aspirin is given, IV access established, and defibrillator pads placed proactively given the risk of malignant dysrhythmia. STEMI alert transmitted to the receiving facility. → Nonsustained VT self-terminates: A brief run of nonsustained VT occurs and self-terminates. The patient remains alert with a palpable pulse throughout. Crew captures the rhythm strip, reassesses pulse and mentation continuously, repeats a 12-lead, and continues STEMI transport.

patientInformation.patientCondition: Crushing substernal chest pain radiating to left arm and jaw

scenarioEvents.name: Initial Contact
scenarioEvents.description: Crew arrives to find a 60-year-old male seated in a recliner, pale and diaphoretic, clutching his chest. He reports crushing chest pain radiating to his left arm and jaw for the past 45 minutes.

scenarioEvents.name: 12-lead, ASA, and IV started
scenarioEvents.description: 12-lead EKG confirms an inferior STEMI. Aspirin is given, IV access established, and defibrillator pads placed proactively given the risk of malignant dysrhythmia. STEMI alert transmitted to the receiving facility.
relatedChecklist: Acquire 12-lead EKG within 10 minutes of patient contact
Transmit STEMI alert with advance notification to receiving facility
Place defibrillator pads proactively given dysrhythmia risk
Nitroglycerin 0.4 mg SL (SBP >100, no PDE5 use in 48h); may repeat q3–5min

scenarioEvents.name: Nonsustained VT self-terminates
scenarioEvents.description: A brief run of nonsustained VT occurs and self-terminates. The patient remains alert with a palpable pulse throughout. Crew captures the rhythm strip, reassesses pulse and mentation continuously, repeats a 12-lead, and continues STEMI transport.
relatedChecklist: Continuously reassess pulse and mental status during any rhythm change
Perform a repeat 12-lead EKG after the rhythm change resolves
Keep defibrillator charged/ready for synchronized cardioversion if VT recurs and sustains

scenarioEvents.name: Defib pads not placed
scenarioEvents.description: A run of VT develops unexpectedly. The crew must interrupt care to attach pads. The rhythm fails to terminate and accelerates, and the patient becomes lightheaded with a weak, thready pulse.
relatedChecklist: Immediately attach pads and perform synchronized cardioversion for unstable VT
Consider sedation and analgesia for the responsive patient before cardioversion

scenarioEvents.name: Pulseless VT — cardiac arrest
scenarioEvents.description: The patient becomes unresponsive and pulseless while still in monomorphic VT. Crew immediately begins high-quality CPR and treats per the shockable cardiac arrest pathway with defibrillation and epinephrine.
relatedChecklist: Initiate high-quality chest compressions immediately (rate 100–120/min, depth 5–6 cm)
Defibrillate per Zoll biphasic setting (120 J first shock) for shockable VT
Give epinephrine 1 mg IV/IO during the first or second round of compressions
